question: Find the shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}+\hat{j})$ and $\vec{r}=\hat{j}+\mu(\hat{i}+\hat{k})$.
explanation:
Step 1: Position and direction vectors
For the first line,
$$\vec{a}_1=\hat{i}+\hat{k},\quad \vec{b}_1=\hat{i}+\hat{j}.$$
For the second line,
$$\vec{a}_2=\hat{j},\quad \vec{b}_2=\hat{i}+\hat{k}.$$
Step 2: Vector joining points on the lines
$$\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}.$$
Step 3: Vector perpendicular to both lines
$$\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2=(\hat{i}+\hat{j})\times(\hat{i}+\hat{k})=\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}.$$
Hence,
$$|\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2|=\sqrt{3}.$$
Step 4: Shortest-distance formula
$$d=\frac{|(\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1)\cdot(\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2)|}{|\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2|}.$$
Therefore,
$$d=\frac{|-1-1+1|}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.$$
Step 5: Final result
The shortest distance between the two lines is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ unit.
